name: EMG-RAG

paper.title: Crafting Personalized Agents through Retrieval-Augmented Generation on Editable Memory Graphs

construction.unit: first-person memory sentence, attached to the entity nodes it mentions
construction.kept_as: LLM-standardized statements from assistant chats and OCR'd app screenshots
construction.processing: assistant filters raw data (auto-classification or user asks to remember); GPT-4 rewrites it as memory sentences with absolute dates and resolved coreference; entity recognition and relation extraction add graph nodes and edges

organization.structure: three layers: 4 memory types -> subclasses (tree) -> entity-relation memory graph
organization.stores: one Editable Memory Graph per user, kept on the device
organization.index: CPT-Text embeddings of memories and questions (Faiss); TransE embeddings of entities, relations and subclasses

management.operations: insert, delete (time-limited memories) or replace, chosen by comparing a new memory with the top-1 memory in its nearest subclass
management.conflicts: replacement rewrites the entity nodes of an existing relation (e.g. a changed departure time)
management.forgetting: deletion of memories valid only until a date (e.g. an expiring voucher)

retrieval.query: question; its entity and relation are extracted for the policy state (method not stated)
retrieval.candidates: top-K=3 memories by embedding similarity activate graph nodes; depth-first walk from each
retrieval.selection: RL policy (2-layer MLP) decides per visited memory: include and go deeper, or stop the branch
retrieval.budget: no fixed number of memories; K=3 start nodes

use.context: question concatenated with the selected memories
use.reasoning: single call to a frozen LLM

classify.note: Structure is a type/subclass tree over an entity graph; retrieval walks the graph, so 'graph'. The set is fixed by a small learned policy (not an LLM, not top-k); 'reranker' is the closest option.

stages.ingestion: Chats with a phone assistant and OCR text of app screenshots; the assistant keeps items it classifies as memorable or that the user asks it to remember.
stages.construction: GPT-4 turns the filtered raw data into standardized first-person memory sentences, with absolute dates and coreference resolved.
stages.organization: Each user gets an Editable Memory Graph: 4 memory types, their subclasses as a tree, and below them an entity graph built by entity and relation extraction; TransE places each entity under its nearest subclass.
stages.update: A new memory is placed in its nearest subclass and compared with the top-1 memory there, then inserted, deleted (time-limited) or used to replace entity nodes.
stages.retrieval: The top-3 memories for the question activate graph nodes; a depth-first walk starts from each, and an RL policy decides at every node whether to include its memory and continue or stop.
stages.answer: A frozen LLM (GPT-4, ChatGLM3-6B or PanGu-38B) answers from the question plus the selected memories.
stages.learning: Only the selection policy is trained: supervised warm start on GPT-4-labelled required memories, then REINFORCE with the change in ROUGE/BLEU of the answer as reward; online fine-tuning on real user questions after deployment.

summary: Organizes a phone user's memories as an editable type/subclass tree over an entity graph and trains a small RL policy to walk the graph and choose which memories to give a frozen LLM, instead of a fixed top-K.
notes:
Venue verified: EMNLP 2024 main, ACL Anthology 2024.emnlp-main.281; arXiv comment 'accepted by EMNLP 2024'. No code: the paper gives no repository and the anthology page lists none; the dataset is a proprietary Huawei assistant dataset. Paper read from arXiv v1 PDF.
DESIGN: §4.1-4.4, §5.1, App. A. control.management = fixed-rule is a best reading: the paper says edits follow from comparing relations of the new and top-1 memories but not who makes the comparison. learning = mixed (supervised warm start + REINFORCE).

sources.code_note: No official code found: none linked in the paper or on the ACL Anthology page, and a GitHub search for EMG-RAG finds only unrelated projects. Everything here is from the paper.

headline: The memory set is chosen by a tiny RL policy walking a user's memory graph, not by top-K; the LLM stays frozen.
Evaluation data, questions and reference answers are all generated by GPT-4 from a proprietary Huawei dataset, and there is no code.

units.name: Memory
units.role: one standardized fact or event about the user
units.made_by: GPT-4 from filtered chats and screenshots

fields.name: memory sentence
fields.what: first-person statement, dates made absolute, coreference resolved

fields.name: embedding
fields.what: CPT-Text vector; also used for subclass partition centres (mean of memory embeddings)

units.name: Entity node and relation edge
units.role: memory graph layer; each in-degree node carries its memory
units.made_by: entity recognition and relation extraction (models not named)

units.name: Type and subclass
units.role: tree over the graph: Relationship, Preference, Event, Attribute and their subclasses

fields.name: subclass
fields.what: e.g. Colleague, Arrangement, Diet preference; entities assigned by TransE nearness

write.how: assistant keeps chat items it classifies as memorable (Active Remember) or that the user asks to keep (Passive Remember); screenshots go through OCR
GPT-4 rewrites raw data into memory sentences; date conversion, anaphora and event coreference resolution
entity recognition for nodes, relation extraction for edges; TransE assigns entities to the closest subclass
embed new memory, find nearest subclass, retrieve top-1 memory in it, then insert, delete or replace by comparing relations

read.how: CPT-Text similarity; nodes of the top memories are activated

depth-first search from each activated node; at each node the policy sees 3 cosine similarities (question entity vs node, question relation vs edge, question vs memory) and outputs include-and-continue or stop

answer_context.sees: the question and the memory sentences the policy selected
answer_context.format: not given beyond concatenation Q ⊕ M

compression.what: answer context vs all user memories
compression.basis: Not reported: the paper gives no counts of selected memories or tokens. Users hold roughly 72-296 new memories per day (App. A.3).

open_questions: Reference answers and 'required memories' come from GPT-4, and GPT-4 is also the answer model; the reward and the metric both favour matching GPT-4's wording.
No run separates the graph (editing, structure) from the learned selector: M-RAG differs in both.

glance.a: A first-person sentence GPT-4 writes from chats or screenshots, tied to entity nodes in a graph.
4 types -> subclasses (a tree) -> an entity-relation graph, one per user.
Yes: insert, delete time-limited memories, or replace entity nodes of an existing relation.
No reranker; a learned RL policy walks the graph from the top-3 matches and decides which memories to include.

glance.q: What does the answer model read?
glance.a: The question plus the selected memory sentences; the LLM is frozen.

discussion.takeaway: Personal-assistant memory needs editing and multi-memory selection; an editable type/subclass/entity graph plus a small RL selector beats fixed top-K RAG on the authors' own assistant data.

claims.claim: EMG-RAG beats all baselines on question answering.
It also helps autofill and user services.
claims.evidence: EM 92.86 autofill, 96.43 reminder, 91.46 travel vs M-RAG 90.87, 93.75, 86.67. Table 2

claims.claim: Editability keeps it ahead as memories change.
claims.evidence: About 10.6% (QA), 9.5% (AF), 9.7% (US) over M-RAG across 4 weeks of edits. Table 3

claims.claim: The policy gradient stage matters most.
claims.evidence: R-1 93.46 -> 90.59 without PG, 92.95 without WS. Table 4

claims.claim: Online fine-tuning on real questions fixes the cold start.

limits: Training is no cheaper than naive RAG because the LLM must be queried during training to obtain rewards.
reading: The ~10% headline comes from the continuous-edit test (Table 3); in the main QA table the ROUGE-L gain over M-RAG is 3.9% (88.06 vs 84.74).
Questions, reference answers and required-memory labels are generated by GPT-4, and GPT-4 is the main answer model, so scores partly measure agreement with GPT-4.
The data is proprietary and there is no code, so no number can be reproduced.
M-RAG is run without its Agent-R, and all baselines are the authors' reimplementations.
The policy sees only three cosine similarities per node, not the memory text; §5.1 sets a 0.99 discount while Eq. 4 assumes no discounting.
The paper does not report how many memories are selected per question or the answer context size.

abstract.text: The paper defines the task of building personalized agents from the memories a user leaves on a smartphone assistant. EMG-RAG turns chats and screenshot text into memory sentences with GPT-4 and stores them in an Editable Memory Graph: a tree of memory types and subclasses over an entity graph that supports insertion, deletion and replacement. To answer, a reinforcement-learning policy walks the graph from the question's best matches and chooses which memories a frozen LLM receives. On the authors' real-world assistant data it improves question answering, form autofill and user services over existing RAG methods by about 10%, and it was deployed in a product assistant.
abstract.note: Summary in our words; the original abstract is on arXiv.
